summary: Summation No. 28 covers January 1948 (with many statistics for November-December 1947). Politically, MacArthur's New Year message, the Katayama coalition's troubles (Social Democratic convention abrogating the four-party pact, Hirano's purge and secession, the arrest of Susumu Hara), abolition of the Home Ministry and the opening of the Second Diet session dominate. The Tokyo war crimes trial reaches the close of the defense, with Tojo's and Shimada's testimony printed at length. Economic sections report record postwar coal output (2,953,200 tons in December), steady gains in industry and textiles limited by power shortages, first postwar export shipments, the 'substitute rice' program, currency and bank totals, and first machine-tool reparations shipments to China and the Netherlands East Indies. Social sections cover epidemic control, public assistance, repatriation, school enrollments and textbook printing, the war-damage survey of art and structures, and press, radio and film activity. A historian will find detailed month-by-month production, trade, labor, finance and health statistics alongside primary-source speeches and trial testimony.
highlights: On 1 January MacArthur's New Year message said the design of a reconstructed Japan was nearing completion and urged the Japanese to 'remain true to the great spiritual revolution'; the Asahi editorial replied that much renovation remained.

The Social Democratic convention voted 366 to 345 on 19 January to abrogate the four-party policy agreement and re-elected Katayama chairman; Rikizo Hirano and 15 colleagues had seceded on 5 January, cutting the party to 124 House seats.

Liberal Representative Susumu Hara was arrested on 31 January for illegal public property transactions after the House Management Committee agreed on 29 January; Hirano was purged on 14 January and indicted on 20 January.

The Second Diet Session opened 21 January with the Emperor present; on 22 January Prime Minister Katayama called 1948 the year of economic reconstruction and promised administrative reorganization, real-wage increases and state-managed elections.

Home Ministry successors (Construction Board, Local Finance Committee, Domestic Affairs Bureau, National Election Management Commission) began operating; the Central Liaison Office was to be abolished 1 February, and 1,146 municipalities had autonomous police by 25 January.

At the International Military Tribunal for the Far East the defense rested on 12 January, with Hideki Tojo's and Shigetaro Shimada's testimony reproduced; ten trials of 29 suspects ended with nine death sentences.

Coal production hit an Occupation peak of 2,953,200 metric tons in December; first postwar exports included a Toyopet automobile to Egypt, raw silk to Egypt and India, and cloisonne and lacquerware to the United States.

The first machine-tool reparations advance transfers left in January: 974 tools (1,694 tons) to China and 600 tools (1,440 tons) to the Netherlands East Indies; currency in circulation reached 218,049,000,000 yen on 31 January.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Google Books and library covers, title page for Summation No. 28 (January 1948), table of contents, and the list of 109 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Monthly digest: no change in SCAP organization, Hirano purge and Diet opening, record coal output, first postwar export shipments, reparations shipments, epidemic control and press activity.

sections.title: Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: GHQ SCAP's non-military organization did not change in January.

sections.title: Political Activities
sections.summary: Digest of New Year messages, Hara's arrest, Hirano's purge, the Social Democratic convention, abolition of the Home Ministry, the Second Diet session and 192 atrocity investigations.

sections.title: Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of agriculture, record coal output of 2,953,200 tons, industrial indexes, first postwar exports, the 'substitute rice' program, bank totals, 974 machine tools to China, and science items.

sections.title: Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of typhus immunization of 1,300,000 people, a 71 percent drop in dysentery, 17,682,938 pupils, textbook printing, 1,130 missionaries, the art war-damage survey and the Osaka SCAP library.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government and politics, public safety and legal affairs, including the war crimes trials with Tojo's and Shimada's testimony reproduced.

sections.title: Government and Politics
sections.summary: MacArthur's New Year message, Hara's arrest and Hirano's purge, the Social Democratic split over the four-party pact, Home Ministry successors, the Kochi governor election and Katayama's 22 January Diet speech.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: MacArthur's and Asahi's New Year statements, hoarded goods drive, Susumu Hara's arrest, and Hirano's purge, indictment and new National Farmers' Union Diet Club.

sections.title: Political Parties
sections.summary: Social Democratic left-wing revolt, convention vote of 366 to 345 for abrogation, Liberal plan for a New Party Formation Preparatory Committee, and Democratic 10-point program.

sections.title: National Government
sections.summary: Plan to abolish the Central Liaison Office on 1 February, new Reparations Board and Repatriation Division, and the 15 January personnel-reduction plan.

sections.title: Local Government
sections.summary: Naomi Momoi won the Kochi governor election 221,475 to 93,100; Supreme Court on 17 January confirmed Tadao Annaka as Miyazaki governor.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Second Session opened 21 January with the Emperor; Katayama's 22 January policy speech, Nagasaki by-election won by Democrat Kadoya, and party vote tables.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Hoarded goods worth 10,680,325 yen found in December, 162,404 offenses in November, prison population down to 79,913, 458 rail mishaps and sharply higher fires, with charts.

sections.title: Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: 532 judges appointed in December, 192 atrocity investigations, ten trials with nine death sentences, and the IMTFE defense including Tojo's and Shimada's testimony.

sections.title: Legal Affairs
sections.summary: 1,414 inferior-court judges appointed to date, Supreme Court caseload, and instructions on private attorney interviews for accused persons.

sections.title: Investigation and Apprehension of Suspected War Criminals
sections.summary: 192 atrocity investigations completed between 24 December and 24 January, and status of apprehensions of suspects.

sections.title: Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Ten trials of 29 suspected war criminals completed in January: nine sentenced to death, four acquitted, the rest imprisoned.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: The defense rested on 12 January, the tribunal ruled on evidence on 14 January, and long excerpts of Tojo's and Shimada's testimony follow.

sections.title: Defense of Hideki Tojo
sections.summary: Tojo's defense, 26 Dec–7 Jan: he accepts political but not criminal responsibility, describes the 1941 Imperial Conferences and the Hull Note, calls the war self-defense, and in cross-examination denies war is a crime.

sections.title: Testimony of Shigetaro Shimada
sections.summary: Shimada, recalled 9 January, denied Togo's claim of a threat at Ichigaya; he said Togo's testimony reflected guilt, and blamed the Foreign Office for the late Pearl Harbor note (delivered 2:10 p.m.).

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Production, trade, labor, price, finance, property control and science statistics for December 1947 and January 1948, including record coal output of 2,953,200 tons and 218,049,000,000 yen in currency.

sections.title: Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: 44,169 cho of land sold to tenants in December, milk and marine landings, fishing vessel and petroleum allocations, flood damage and an antarctic whaling catch of 354.5 blue whale units.

sections.title: Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Log production of 54,587,020 cubic feet, forest survey (19,687,243 accessible hectares), record coal output of 2,953,200 tons, crude oil and mineral production.

sections.title: Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke up 8,660 tons, cement 132,699 tons, plus steel, shipbuilding, chemicals, machine tools, locomotives, rolling stock and textile machinery output tables.

sections.title: Manufacturing
sections.summary: Trucks up 76 percent and a postwar high in sewing machines, with food, alcohol, tobacco, paper, glass, optical and medical instruments, rubber, leather and agricultural implements.

sections.title: Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton, silk, rayon and wool output limited by electric power; raw silk stocks of 110,857 bales; cloth, spindle, loom and knit goods tables.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Commercial vehicle operating ratio down one percent, railway freight down about five percent, coastal cargo down 9.5 percent, electric power generation up three percent, gas consumption up 13.7 percent.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: 8 January radio receiver standards ordinance, radiotelegraph rates, postal insurance maximum raised to 25,000 yen, equipment output, and a December Ministry deficit of 347,011,466 yen.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: 26,421 unions with 5,993,613 members on 30 November, calm January labor relations, government and coal worker wage talks, a labor press of over 100 publications, and employment statistics.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: December trade tables; first postwar exports including a Toyopet to Egypt; 1947 totals of 360,892,000 yards of cotton cloth and 759,093 tons of salt imported.

sections.title: Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Staple-food purchases and quota fulfillment, the 'substitute rice' program begun in January, December sugar distribution of 22,394 tons, tobacco price increases and ten rationed commodities.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Currency of 218,049,000,000 yen, Reconstruction Finance Bank loans of 44,210,356,000 yen, national debt of 374,957,000,000 yen, plus bank deposits, liquidation proceeds, tax collections and local finance.

sections.title: Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: 1,813,965,000 yen of neutral and Allied property reported, German property freeze lifted for nonobjectionable nationals, 4,371 companies under holding company control, and reparations shipments.

sections.title: Science and Technology
sections.summary: Renewal Committee on science organization, 6,563,600 yen in grants to 19 institutes, 46 patents granted, and Rebun Island eclipse expedition plans.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, then education, religion, cultural resources and media of expression, including typhus immunization of 1,300,000 and 17,682,938 pupils enrolled.

sections.title: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Typhus immunization of over 1,300,000, dysentery down 71 percent, communicable disease tables, milk inspection, medical supplies, narcotics, public assistance, repatriation and vital statistics.

sections.title: Education, Religion, Cultural Resources and Media of Expression
sections.summary: 17,682,938 pupils enrolled, 141,790,968 textbooks printed, 1,130 foreign missionaries, 1.5 percent of art objects and 13 percent of structures war damaged, plus press, radio, film and library news.

sections.title: Map of Japan and back matter
sections.summary: Map of Japan showing administrative regions and prefectures, followed by library catalogue label and back covers.
